notes: POWO accepts A. quadrifidus and three infraspecific taxa, including var. wrightii.
Central Texas horticultural/floristic references commonly use A. quadrifidus var. wrightii; Deep Review should decide whether the learner entry should be at species or variety rank.

target_zone_range_leads.guardrail: Research-only. Deep Review must verify accepted taxonomy and exact target-zone native counties; no county inference.
leads: POWO lists Texas within the native range of the species.
Master Plant Pool has one personal iNaturalist source but no current Hays Local flag.
NPSOT backlog separately lists var. wrightii.
Purola Hays Flora explicitly says its var. wrightii plant was introduced from seed, so that site record cannot establish native Hays occurrence.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with growth form: this is the woody shrub in the batch, with opposite lanceolate leaves and terminal spike-like panicles of long scarlet-orange tubular flowers.
diagnostic_traits: terminal spike-like panicles of condensed cymes
scarlet to orange-red long tubular bilabiate flowers
local Central Texas material often treated as var. wrightii

confusers.separator: Flame acanthus is a woody shrub with red tubular flowers; R. metziae is a small herb with large white petunia-like flowers.
